results.memory: Production deploys of the api gateway go through the deploy-gateway GitHub Actions workflow. A deploy is a tagged release pushed to the default branch, never a manual apply from a laptop.
The billing service writes to the billing-db-blue cluster. Reads for reporting go to its replica, writes never bypass the service.
The auth service listens on port 8443 inside the cluster; the ingress terminates TLS and forwards to that port.
The data pipeline is orchestrated by Airflow; every DAG lives in the pipelines repo and is deployed with the scheduler image.
Crashes from the courier mobile app are reported to Sentry; the mobile team triages them in the weekly quality review.
Production workloads run on the prod-hlx-1 Kubernetes cluster; the platform team owns its upgrades.
CI jobs run on the runners-medium pool; the pool autoscales between two and twenty machines.
The web repo is formatted with prettier, run from the pre-commit hook and checked in CI.
The default branch of the platform repo is mainline; feature branches are rebased onto it before merge.
Customer data exports are written to the hlx-exports-prod bucket with a thirty-day lifecycle rule.
Order events are published to orders-topic-v1; consumers must be idempotent because the broker delivers at least once.
Session state is cached in the cache-alpha cluster; entries expire after twelve hours.
On-call pages are sent through PagerDuty; the rotation is weekly and hands over on the release day.
The public API allows 1200 requests per minute per key; the limiter returns 429 above that.
The web monorepo uses pnpm for dependency management; the lockfile is committed and CI installs with a frozen lockfile.
Feature flags are served by LaunchDarkly; every flag has an owner and a removal date.
Service metrics are shipped to Datadog; dashboards are defined as code in the observability repo.
The weekly release train leaves on Tuesday; anything merged after the cut waits a week.
The engineering docs site is built with MkDocs from the docs directory of each repo.
Backend services run on Python 3.11; the base image pins it and CI tests that version only.
Single sign-on for internal tools goes through Okta; groups there map to service roles.
Container images are pushed to ghcr.io/halden; production pulls by digest, never by tag.
Cluster ingress is handled by ingress-nginx; TLS certificates are issued by the cert manager.
Logs are shipped from every node by fluent-bit, which runs as a daemonset.
Invoice PDFs in the billing service are rendered with wkhtmltopdf from an HTML template.
The auth service hashes passwords with argon2id; the parameters are tuned to about a quarter second per hash.
The analytics pipeline loads into BigQuery; the warehouse is partitioned by event day.
The iOS bundle identifier of the courier mobile app is com.halden.courier; it is shared between the store build and the internal build.
The staging environment is reachable at staging.halden.dev behind the VPN.
The SLO policy is written up in runbooks/slo-policy.md in the platform repo.
Billing database backups are written to the hlx-backups-eu bucket every six hours.
Default reviewers for the platform repo are defined in the CODEOWNERS file at the repo root.
The api gateway canary is watched on the gateway-canary-v1 dashboard during every rollout.
The courier mobile app is built by Bitrise; signing certificates are stored in its secrets.
Transactional email is sent through SendGrid; templates live in the notifications repo.
Card payments are processed by Stripe; webhooks are verified with the signing secret from the secret store.
The primary deployment region is eu-west-1; the secondary region only runs read replicas.
Distributed traces are stored in Jaeger; sampling is one in ten requests.
The customer web app is hosted on Vercel with preview deployments per pull request.
Incidents are coordinated in the incidents-hlx channel; the incident commander posts the timeline there.
The deploy workflow reads the AWS access key from the CI secret store; the key value is never written into the repo or the runbooks.
Passwords for the staging admin panel live in the team password manager under the Platform folder; ask the on-call lead for access.
As of the 2026 platform review the billing service is the only service still on the legacy event schema, and migrating it is scheduled for the next quarter.
The API keys for the shipping-rate provider rotate every ninety days; rotation is automated by the rotate-keys job and nobody handles the values by hand.
Right now the data pipeline runs a nightly backfill while the warehouse migration is in progress, and the backfill will be removed when it completes.
Internal service auth uses a JWT signed with an RS256 key held by the auth service; example payloads with placeholder signatures are in docs/auth.md.
The api gateway deploy workflow was renamed: production deploys now run through release-gateway in GitHub Actions. The tagging convention did not change.
Billing cut over to the billing-db-green cluster after the storage migration; the previous cluster is decommissioned and the service writes only to the new one.
The auth service moved to port 9443 when the sidecar was introduced; the ingress forwards to 9443 and the old port is closed.
The data pipeline was migrated to Dagster. The scheduler and every job definition now run there; the previous orchestrator was switched off after the parallel run.
Mobile crash reporting switched to Bugsnag with the new SDK release; the mobile team now triages crashes there.
Production moved to the prod-hlx-2 cluster during the control-plane upgrade; the previous cluster was drained and deleted afterwards.
CI jobs were moved to the runners-large pool because the integration suite ran out of memory on the smaller machines.
The web repo adopted biome as its formatter and linter; the old formatter config was removed and CI checks biome output.
The platform repo's default branch was renamed to trunkline as part of the monorepo consolidation; branch protection moved with it.
Exports now land in the hlx-exports-v2 bucket, which has object versioning on; the previous bucket is read-only.
Order events moved to orders-topic-v3 with the schema change; producers stopped writing to the old topic once every consumer had migrated.
Session caching moved to the cache-bravo cluster, which runs in the same availability zones as the services; the previous cache cluster was retired.
Paging moved to Opsgenie when the contract was renegotiated; the rotation schedule was imported unchanged.
The public API rate limit was raised to 3600 requests per minute per key after the gateway capacity upgrade.
The web monorepo switched to yarn workspaces; the old lockfile was deleted and CI installs with yarn in immutable mode.
Feature flags were migrated to a self-hosted Unleash instance; the flag ownership rules carried over.
Metrics and traces now go to Honeycomb; the dashboards were rebuilt there and the previous backend account was closed.
The release train moved to Thursday so that fixes from the Monday support review make the same week's release.
The docs site was rebuilt on Docusaurus to get versioned docs; the previous generator config was removed.
The backend services were upgraded to Python 3.13 with the new base image; CI tests 3.13 only.
Single sign-on moved to Keycloak during the tenant consolidation; the group-to-role mapping was recreated there.
Images now live in the private registry at harbor.halden.internal; the public registry namespace is frozen and production pulls from the private one by digest.
Ingress was replaced by traefik to get native canary routing; the certificate setup is unchanged.
Log shipping moved to vector-agent, which replaced the daemonset and adds sampling for debug logs.
The canary dashboard was replaced by gateway-canary-v2, which adds per-region error panels.
Mobile builds moved to Codemagic for the trial period; the signing setup was copied over.
Transactional email switched to Postmark to improve deliverability; the templates were ported.
Card payments were moved to Adyen as part of the European expansion.
The primary region moved to eu-central-1 for data residency reasons.
Tracing moved to Tempo to cut storage cost; the collectors were reconfigured.
The customer web app moved to Netlify during the pricing review.
Incident coordination moved to a dedicated sev-room channel with restricted membership.
Invoice PDFs are archived for seven years under the finance retention policy, and the archive is read-only.
The auth service limits login attempts to five per minute per account and locks the account for an hour after that.
Warehouse dashboards refresh hourly and the analytics team owns their definitions.
The courier mobile app ships on a two-week cadence through TestFlight before each store release.
Staging is redeployed every night at 02:00 UTC from the default branch, and its database is reset weekly.
SLO reviews happen monthly with the platform lead, and error budget burn is reported at the review.
Backups are exercised by a quarterly restore drill, and the drill result is filed with the audit evidence.
